newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch state plans no new bond issues in Q3 1997.
newsitem.headline: Dutch state plans no new bond issues in Q3 1997.

text.p: The Dutch government said on Monday it did not plan any new bond issues in the third quarter of 1997.
But the Dutch Finance Ministry's capital markets agency said it would continue to issue nine percent January 15, 2001 and 7.5 percent January 15, 2023 bonds on a continuous tap basis.

The agency said earlier this year it planned to reopen tap sales of these two state loans, raising up to 3.0 billion guilders in each in 1997. At June 30, 2.227 billion guilders of the January 2001 bonds and 1.881 billion guilders of the January 2023 bonds had been issued.
In May, the agency said 4.5 billion guilders of the government's 1997 borrowing requirement of 37.4 billion guilders remained.
This excluded the 6.0 billion guilders to be raised in 1997 from the reopening of the 2001 and 2023 bonds.
